Initial availability is planned in English in the United States, Australia, Canada, India, New Zealand, Singapore, South Africa, and the United Kingdom.

Should You Buy HomePod Mini or HomePod Mini 2?

The ‌HomePod mini 2‌ should be the default choice for most new buyers when the price difference is small. If remaining original stock costs $129, paying another $20 provides the new Mac and surround sound capabilities, faster connectivity, Sound Glow, and eligibility for the forthcoming ‌Siri‌ AI update.

A substantially discounted original ‌HomePod‌ mini remains worth considering for straightforward music playback or adding smart home control to another room. Its value is strongest when you will use the shared features and have little interest in the new features.

title: Every new Apple product coming in 2026 & 2027
content:
Macworld





It’s been a huge year for Apple, with a wave of new products arriving throughout 2026. The year began with the MacBook Neo and iPhone 17e in March, followed by the new Mac mini and Mac Studio in August.
September brought another major wave of launches at Apple’s “Surprise and Shine” event, including the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max, iPhone Duo, Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, and AirPods 5.
Then on October 13 the company held a “Welcome Home” gathering at which new smart-home products debuted including HomeView, HomePod mini 2, a new Apple TV 4K and the Apple Home Collection.
Apple has also rolled out its major operating-system updates for 2026, including iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27, alongside updates for the Apple Watch, Apple TV, and Vision Pro.
But Apple isn’t finished yet. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that further Mac and iPad announcements are planned for October 27, although Apple has yet to confirm that date.
With most of Apple’s biggest launches already behind us, attention is turning to what’s next. Here’s what’s still to come.
Apple’s roadmap: At a glance
As of September 1, 2026, Apple’s roadmap has come under the direction of CEO John Ternus. Former CEO Tim Cook has moved into the executive chairman role. The shift from an operations-focused leader to one with deep hardware engineering roots could signal a more product-driven approach – and a renewed emphasis on standout hardware. 


ProductExpected timingKey rumoursShould you wait?

iPad miniOctober 27 announcement rumoredA20 Pro, improved water resistance, bigger displayYes
MacBook Pro with TouchscreenOctober 27 announcement rumoredOLED touchscreen, lighter designYes, if you want a redesign 
iMac October 27 announcement rumoredM6 chip, possible new colorsYes
M6 14-inch MacBook ProOctober 27 announcement rumoredM6 upgrade to the entry-level modelYes
Apple Smart GlassesPreview in late 2026 possibleCameras, audio, Siri/Visual IntelligenceYes
iPhone 18/iPhone Air 2Spring 2027iPhone 18 could merge with iPhone AirYes
iPhone 18eSpring 2027Possible Dynamic IslandNo
iPadSpring 2027Apple Intelligence supportYes

 






Every New Apple Product Launched in 2026… so far
Here is what Apple has already announced in 2026:
HomeView: A new smart-home display with a 7-inch touchscreen, available in tabletop and wall-mounted versions.
HomePod mini 2: An updated speaker with an S10 chip, new colors and Siri AI coming through a future software update.
Apple TV 4K: A fourth-generation model with an A19 chip and an updated Siri Remote.
Apple Home Collection: Cameras, doorbells, locks and thermostats developed with accessory partners.
iPhone Duo: Apple’s first foldable iPhone: iPhone Duo Guide.
iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max: A20 Pro chip, upgraded vapor-chamber cooling, camera improvements: iPhone 18 Pro & Max Guide.
Apple Watch Series 12 & Ultra 4: Faster chips, Apple’s latest health-sensing features: Apple Watch Series 12 & Ultra 4.
AirPods 5: Stronger open-ear Active Noise Cancellation and longer battery life: AirPods 5.
Mac mini M6 and M5 Pro: Faster storage, upgraded connectivity, and a strong focus on AI performance: New Mac mini 2026 guide.
Mac Studio M5 Max and M5 Ultra: Faster AI and graphics performance, increased memory bandwidth: New Mac Studio 2026 guide.
AirPods Max 2: Improved audio and the H2 chip. Find out more here: AirPods Max 2 guide.
MacBook Neo: Apple’s brand new, low-cost Mac laptop. Find out more here: MacBook Neo guide.
MacBook Air M5: Now with the M5 chip. Read about the 2026 MacBook Air here: MacBook Air M5 guide.
MacBook Pro M5 Pro & M5 Max: A significant upgrade over the M4 series. Read: MacBook Pro M5 Pro & Max guide.
Studio Display: Finally gets Thunderbolt 5 and a better webcam. 
Studio Display XDR: With mini-LED technology and ProMotion up to 120Hz.
iPhone 17e: The new, entry-level, iPhone replaces the iPhone 16e. Read more here: iPhone 17e guide.
iPad Air M4: The iPad Air now has an M4 chip. Read more here: iPad Air M4 guide.
AirTag 2: Four years on Apple updated the AirTag, read our review here: AirTag 2nd gen review.
And… RIP Mac Pro: Apple has confirmed that it is discontinuing its tower workstation.  
Read on to find out what new products to expect at Apple’s next event and throughout 2026.


						

							







Every New Apple Product Launching in 2026
In the sections below we’ve split the upcoming new products into categories including Mac, iPad, iPhone, Apple Watch, Home, AirPods, and some new product categories.
Apple Intelligence and Siri updates still coming in 2026
Apple released iOS 27, iPadOS 27 and its other major software updates in September, bringing the new Siri AI experience, expanded Apple Intelligence features, parental controls and a range of improvements across Apple’s apps and operating systems.
But Apple’s 2026 software rollout isn’t finished. Siri AI is still being rolled out to eligible users, with access depending on device, language and region, and Apple has already begun testing the updates that will follow the initial iOS 27 and macOS 27 releases.
Siri and Apple Intelligence
Siri AI arrived with iOS 27 as a substantially redesigned version of Apple’s voice assistant, with improved conversational abilities, personal-context awareness, onscreen awareness and the ability to carry out more actions across apps. However, not every Apple device can run the new features, and some users may still need to join a waiting list before gaining access.
Apple is also expanding Siri AI beyond its initial English-language launch. Additional language support is due during the remainder of 2026, while regional restrictions mean some Apple Intelligence and Siri AI features remain unavailable in parts of the world. 
Upcoming iOS 27 and macOS updates
iOS 27 itself is already available, but Apple is continuing development through iOS 27.x updates. These releases are expected to deliver additional features, refinements and bug fixes throughout the remainder of 2026, with Apple’s beta program providing an early indication of what is coming next.
The same applies to iPadOS 27, macOS 27, watchOS 27 and Apple’s other platforms, which will continue to receive point updates following their initial September releases. Find out about the latest iOS beta and latest macOS beta.  


						

							


What new iPads are coming in 2026/2027 

				
					

				
			
Screenshot

Foundry




Don’t expect major redesigns for the iPads this year. Instead, Apple is likely to focus on faster chips and other internal upgrades. That said, both the iPad and iPad mini are due for an update – particularly the entry-level iPad, which currently lacks support for Apple Intelligence. Here’s what we expect Apple to announce:
iPad mini
Expected announcement: October 27, according to Bloomberg; unconfirmed.
The next iPad mini could be one of Apple’s biggest remaining upgrades of the year. Multiple reports point to Apple replacing the current 8.3-inch LCD with an OLED display, potentially increasing the screen size slightly to around 8.5 inches while keeping the overall dimensions much the same. Samsung Display is also reported to have begun mass-producing OLED panels for the new model, suggesting the launch is getting closer.
The latest reporting points to the A20 Pro chip – as used in the iPhone 18 Pro. Earlier references suggested the A19 Pro, but more recent findings in Apple code favor the newer processor. 
Other upgrades could include Apple’s N1 networking chip, bringing Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread, while cellular models are expected to adopt Apple’s C1X modem. Apple may also move the front camera to the landscape edge, bringing the iPad mini into line with the rest of the current iPad range.
Apple is also reportedly working on a more water-resistant design. Bloomberg has reported that this could involve a new vibration-based speaker system that would allow Apple to eliminate conventional speaker holes and improve sealing. Bloomberg points to an October 27 announcement, although Apple has not confirmed the date. Read our round up of iPad mini rumors.
iPad (12th generation)
Early 2027 expected
When Apple updated the standard iPad in March 2025, the biggest disappointment was its A16 chip, which doesn’t support Apple Intelligence. The next model is expected to address that with an A18 or A19 chip, bringing Apple’s AI features to its entry-level tablet.
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman previously predicted a 2026 launch but now expects the new iPad in the first quarter of 2027 at the earliest. Read more in our new iPad rumor roundup.
Should you buy now or wait? 
With the iPad prices increasing in June 2026, you may want to hold off buying one now. If you are going to pay more at least get the most up-to-date model, or buy from Apple’s Refurbished Store to get a bargain. Read Should I buy an iPad now or wait?


						

							


Which new Macs are coming in 2026/2027?
2026 is expected to be a significant year for the Mac, with Apple’s first touchscreen Mac rumored as part of a MacBook Pro redesign. March 3 saw the launch of the M5 MacBook Air and M5 Pro/M5 Max MacBook Pro and March 4 saw Apple introduce a new entry-level laptop – the $599 MacBook Neo.
The long expected Mac Studio and Mac mini updates came in August 2026 and went on sale September 22, although some high-memory Mac Studio configurations won’t arrive until later. These Macs have become popular for running AI models locally; however, global RAM shortages – driven by AI companies purchasing large amounts of memory for data centres – have been having a knock-on effect on availability during 2026 and these RAM shortages have also had an effect on prices, with Mac prices increasing by $300 to $500 in June and in the case of the Mac mini, by a further $100 with the 2026 launch.
One Mac that won’t be getting an update is the long-neglected Mac Pro. Apple has confirmed that the Mac Pro will be discontinued in favor of the Mac Studio.
Touchscreen MacBook Pro
Expected announcement: October 27, according to Bloomberg; unconfirmed.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Apple’s redesigned MacBook Pro is expected to feature an OLED touchscreen and a substantially lighter body. However, Mark Gurman has played down earlier suggestions that it will be significantly thinner. Reports point to the use of M5 Pro and M5 Max processors to enable Apple to keep the project on schedule.
Read the rumors about the MacBook Pro with a touch screen.
M6 MacBook Pro 
Expected announcement: October 27, according to Bloomberg; unconfirmed.
Apple is expected to update the entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro with an M6 chip. This would be a separate update from the rumored OLED touchscreen MacBook Pro, which is expected to use M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.
Gurman includes this model among the products reportedly planned for October 27. 
Read more about the rumored M6 MacBook Pro.
iMac
Expected announcement: October 27, according to Bloomberg; unconfirmed.
Apple is reportedly preparing an M6 iMac, skipping the M5 generation following the M4 model introduced in October 2024. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman expects the update before the end of 2026, with new color options but no major redesign.
Gurman’s October 8 report specifically named the M6 iMac among the products planned for October 27. 
Read more about the rumored M6 iMac and new colors. Also read about the larger iMac rumors.
Should you buy now or wait? 
With the prices of Macs increasing in June due to the global RAM shortages you may want to hold off buying one now. If you are going to pay more at least get the most up-to-date model, or buy from Apple’s Refurbished Store to get a bargain. Read the following for more guidance:
Should you buy the MacBook Pro now or wait? 
Should you buy the MacBook Air now or wait?
Should you buy a Mac mini now or wait?
Should you buy a Mac Studio now or wait?


						

							


AirPod updates coming in 2027
According to a brief update in Mark Gurman’s Power On newsletter for Bloomberg in August, Apple is aiming to launch camera-equipped AirPods.
The new earbuds are expected to resemble the AirPods Pro 3, although it’s not yet clear whether they will also include a heart rate sensor.
The cameras are said to include both visible-light and infrared sensors, but they reportedly won’t be designed for taking photos or recording video, as their placement and image quality would make them unsuitable for those tasks. Instead, the cameras are expected to enable AI-powered features, such as hand gesture recognition, adapting audio based on the surrounding environment, and detecting whether someone is speaking directly to you or simply talking nearby.


						

							


Apple smart home products coming in 2027
In October 2026 Apple announced a major expansion of its smart-home lineup with the launch of the HomeView, HomePod mini 2, a new Apple TV 4K and the Apple Home Collection at its “Welcome Home” experience. We are still waiting for the update to the larger HomePod, with hope that could arrive in 2027.
HomePod 3
Expected: 2027 or later
Apple has also been linked with a more advanced HomePod featuring a built-in display. This is sometimes referred to in reports as the HomePod Touch, although that is not an official Apple name.
Unlike the HomeView, which primarily functions as a standalone smart-home hub, this device is expected to combine a traditional HomePod speaker with a touchscreen display. 
Reports have also described more ambitious versions with a display mounted on a robotic arm, although those appear to be further away.


						

							


What new iPhones are coming in 2027?

				
					

				
			There are new iPhones coming.
Foundry




Based on current industry analysis and supply chain information, Apple has some significant changes planned for the iPhone in 2027, with an 20th anniversary iPhone rumored as well as the iPhone 18, 18e and iPhone Air 2.
iPhone 18 & iPhone 18e
Spring 2027 launch expected
Reports suggest that Apple could delay the iPhone 18 and release that handset alongside the iPhone 18e in the spring of 2027.
iPhone Air 2
The iPhone Air could also be getting an update. But there are rumors that it will actually merge with the iPhone 18. See our iPhone Air 2 rumors.
Should you buy now or wait? 
With the iPhone 18 launch not expected until the spring, now is a good time to buy an iPhone 17. Read: When is the best time to buy an iPhone.
However, prices have already risen across the board, so it is no longer possible to beat the price hikes unless you find a refurbished iPhone.


						

							


Upcoming Vision devices, AR and spatial computing
Apple Smart Glasses 
Possible 2026 introduction, 2027 launch
Unlike the bulky Vision Pro headset, the upcoming smart glasses from Apple are expected to follow a form factor similar to the Ray-Ban Meta glasses. This will be Apple’s first product built specifically for “Visual Intelligence.” It will likely handle tasks such as live translations, music playback, phone calls, and turn-by-turn directions. Apple could provide a first glimpse or “preview” of the glasses by the end of 2026. 
Vision Pro
Possible 2027 update
Prior to 2026, Apple’s spatial computing strategy has focused on the high-end market, but reports indicate a more affordable version of the headset is in development. Apple has reportedly paused work on a successor to the high-end Vision Pro and will instead release a cheaper Vision Pro.

title: Apple just made my decision to buy an iPhone Duo much easier
content:
Macworld





When iOS 27 rolled out earlier this month, it included an intriguing new feature called iPhone Handoff. The feature wasn’t exactly new—it had already been mentioned in a footnote on the iOS 27 page back in June — but there weren’t many details about how it would work until it arrived. 
The idea here is to use the same SIM card and phone number on two iPhones at the same time. Think of it as how the cellular Apple Watch works, but on the iPhone. On the surface, it seems to be an extremely niche purpose, useful for people who have one iPhone for personal use and another for work. But with the launch of the iPhone Duo looming, iPhone Handoff seems to have an entirely different user in mind.
The two-iPhone dilemma
You see, even months before Apple launched the iPhone Duo, some were already speculating that this feature would come at just the right time. That’s because we now have not just one, but two new flagship iPhones — and they’re quite different from each other. Most people will probably choose one or the other, especially since they’re both expensive. But Apple knows there’s a group of enthusiasts who will likely end up with both — and I’m one of them.
The iPhone Duo is by far the most exciting product of this iPhone season. It’s a brand new form factor that opens up new possibilities. Even if you’re not a fan of foldables, chances are you’ll at least want to see this device in person to get a feel for it. 
The thing is, while it costs the most, the Duo isn’t exactly the best iPhone in the lineup. Because it’s so thin, Apple had to make some compromises. There’s no Face ID or telephoto camera on the back. For “pro” users, this could be a significant drawback. But the Duo alone has advantages over other iPhones, and that’s where some people might want to get both — maybe a Duo for professional work, and an 18 Pro for fun.

				
					

				
			
iPhone Handoff makes it easy to switch between two phones without needing a separate number.

Roman Loyola / Foundry




But having two iPhones has historically been a nightmare. I know this because I already have two. Even if you use iCloud, there’s still one thing that doesn’t sync between them: your phone number. That means you need two different phone lines to keep two iPhones with you. Not only is this inconvenient, but it also adds a significant extra cost on your monthly wireless bill. 
iPhone Handoff is here to change that. It finally allows two iPhones to share the same phone line. But how does it work?
How Apple solved the problem
As I mentioned earlier, the concept of iPhone Handoff pretty much works the same an iPhone-cellular Apple Watch tandem. Currently, if you have an Apple Watch with LTE or 5G, it already uses your iPhone’s SIM card. Essentially, it detects when your iPhone is out of range and automatically swaps your eSIM to the Apple Watch. This lets you stay connected to your 5G network to receive calls, send messages, and so on. As soon as your iPhone comes back within range, your SIM card switches back to it. Everything happens automatically and is invisible to the user. 
iPhone Handoff works the same way. Your two iPhones will detect which one is currently in use and automatically activate the eSIM on that device. No need to manually swap SIM cards or have two phone lines. This will make owning two iPhones much easier, whether you need them for work or just don’t want to give up your telephoto camera. Again, not everyone will do this, but it’s nice that Apple had this in mind for those who will.

				
					

				
			
If you’re debating whether to buy an iPhone Duo, iPhone Handoff might convince you.

Apple




Of course, not everything is perfect, and iPhone Handoff is launching with quite a few limitations. The feature is currently available to T-Mobile customers in the U.S. and Telekom customers in Germany — and that’s it. Also, T-Mobile is charging an extra $5 per month for iPhone Handoff. It’s certainly cheaper than paying for an extra line, but it’s still not something you can use for free. 
Apple says more carriers will support iPhone Handoff in the coming months, but the truth is there are no further details on what to expect. AT&T recently suggested that it has no plans to support iPhone Handoff anytime soon, so availability might be very limited for a while.
Still, I’m glad Apple came up with a solution for this. Eventually, I’m sure more carriers will start supporting iPhone Handoff, especially if they see that there’s some kind of demand from people who want to have two iPhones. Until the iPhone Duo has the same camera hardware as the iPhone Pro, I’ll probably be one of those people walking around with two iPhones.

title: iOS 27: What’s new, what’s in the latest beta and what’s coming next
content:
Macworld





Apple unveiled iOS 27 at WWDC on June 8, 2026, with the public release following on September 14. But more features are on the way, and the latest beta offers a preview of what’s coming next.
iOS 27 mainly focuses on three key areas: Siri AI, a rebuilt assistant with its own dedicated app; new child safety and parental controls; and system improvements designed to make everyday tasks faster and easier.
iOS 27 supports the iPhone 11 and later, plus the iPhone SE (2nd generation) and later, although some Apple Intelligence and Siri features require newer hardware.
This guide covers iOS 27’s biggest new features, compatible iPhones and the latest beta developments. We also explain what’s expected in the next update, when it could arrive and which features are still to come.


What’s New in iOS 27 at a Glance
Siri AI: Apple’s new Siri AI combines personal context, onscreen awareness and web knowledge to deliver more natural conversations, richer answers, app actions and cross-device chat history.
Apple Intelligence across apps: Apple Intelligence expands across Safari, Photos, Messages, Mail, Calendar, Home and Shortcuts, adding smarter suggestions, automation, image generation and context-aware assistance.
Smarter Photos editing: Photos gains Spatial Reframing, Extend and an upgraded Clean Up tool, allowing users to improve composition, expand images and remove distractions more naturally.
Child safety and parental controls: New parental controls include Ask to Browse, Time Allowances, app schedules and enhanced Communication Safety tools. Activating the redesigned experience through Family Sharing requires every eligible family device to be running version 27 or later.
System Improvements: Apple has made many system operations faster and more efficient, which will be especially noticeable on older phones. Battery life may be longer, and there are dozens of small quality-of-life improvements throughout the system and its apps.
iPhone Handoff: iPhone Handoff in iOS 27 lets two eSIM-equipped iPhones share one number, switching calls, messages and Find My location when unlocked. It requires matching Apple Accounts and carrier support. T-Mobile offers it; Verizon and EE plan support. Fees may apply. More information below.


						

							


iOS 27 latest version: What’s in iOS 27.0.1
The first update was iOS 27.0.1, released on September 28. It fixes unexpected restarts following failed Face ID authentication, a 2x-camera color artifact affecting iPhone 18 Pro models, and an iOS 27 touchscreen freeze triggered by opening Notification Center and Control Center simultaneously.
iOS 27.0.1 also has a preventive role in a cellular problem that Apple did not mention in its published release notes. Apple has confirmed that a small number of iPhone 18 Pro Max models on AT&T can lose cellular service, preventing calls, texts and data access and potentially affecting 911 calls. Some owners reported their phones dropping into SOS mode despite previously showing a strong 5G signal.
Apple says affected iPhone 18 Pro Max owners on AT&T should install iOS 27.0.1 along with a new carrier settings update, which together are intended to prevent the problem. The carrier update should install automatically within 14 days, or users can check for it by going to Settings > General > About. However, the updates cannot repair phones that have already been affected: Apple says devices that have lost service because of the issue cannot be reactivated through software and will need to be replaced through Apple or AT&T.
The iPhone Duo will ship with iOS 27.1. Apple has not confirmed whether other iPhones will receive that version; iOS 27.2 is currently in beta. The iPhone Duo is due to go on sale on October 23.
After that, iOS 27.2 is expected to be the next major update and is currently in beta.


						

							


iOS 27 beta – What’s coming next?
Latest beta: iOS 27.2 
It seems that Apple will only use iOS 27.1 number for the iPhone Duo’s release.
The iOS 27.2 beta 1 was released on September 16, followed by 27.2 beta 2 on September 21. The public beta of iOS 27.2 arrived on September 22. Developer beta 3, was released October 5. Developer beta 4 arrived on October 13. 
When iOS 27.2 arrives it is expected to introduce the following:
Bug fixes and performance improvements addressing issues in iOS 27.
Additional Siri AI languages, including French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish.
Suggested replies in Messages, previously removed before iOS 27 launched.
Automatic password changes for compromised passwords.
Apple has confirmed that the HomeView will require iOS 27.2 to set up when it arrived on November 13, so we can infer that iOS 27.2 will arrive by that date. 
The iOS 27.2 beta had included a Redesigned Health app with AI-powered health insights, however this was removed from from iOS 27.2 beta 4. Apple promises the new Health app will be available later in 2026. 


						

							


What features are still to come in iOS 27
At the time of the launch of iOS 27 not all of Apple’s promised features were available. Missing features include: 
Redesigned Health app: A completely redesigned Health app with AI-powered health insights is coming later in 2026.
Additional Siri AI languages: Siri AI launched in English only. French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish are due in October. 
Smarter suggested replies in Messages: Suggested replies that better reflect the user’s writing style appeared during beta testing but were removed before the public release. 
Automatic password changes: The ability for the Passwords app to visit supported websites and automatically replace compromised passwords was removed shortly before release. 
SynthID identification for AI images: Apple said support for adding SynthID identification to most AI-generated or edited images would arrive in a software update later in 2026. 


						

							


What does Siri AI do in iOS 27

				
					

				
			
Apple




By far the biggest upgrade in iOS 27 is Siri AI – an entirely new architecture for Siri. Apple says it is more personal, conversational, and capable than the current assistant, with support for natural follow-up questions, personal context, onscreen awareness and up-to-date information from the web.
Siri AI features
More natural conversations: Siri AI can understand open-ended questions, follow-up requests and more complex natural language, making interactions feel less like issuing simple voice commands.
Personal context: Siri can draw on information stored in Messages, Mail, Photos and Notes to find details and answer questions. For example, you could ask it to find information buried in an old email or message.
Onscreen awareness: Siri can understand what you’re viewing and act on it, such as saving an address from a message, adding an event to Calendar or answering questions about an article.
Camera intelligence: A new Siri Camera mode lets you show Siri something through the iPhone’s camera, then ask questions or perform actions based on what it sees.
More capable app actions: Siri can perform tasks within apps such as Messages, Music and Reminders. It can, for example, edit a recently sent message, add a song to a playlist or handle more complex Apple Music requests.
Better general knowledge and web answers: Siri can use information from the web to answer questions about recent events and tackle more specific or complicated queries than before.
Conversation history across devices: A dedicated Siri app lets users revisit previous conversations, pin important chats and continue conversations across Apple devices using iCloud syncing.
More natural Siri voices: Siri gains more expressive voices, with controls on compatible devices for adjusting speaking pace and expressiveness. Voice customization requires an iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone Air or newer.
Improved dictation: Better speech recognition, automatic punctuation, capitalization and formatting allow users to dictate more naturally when converting speech into text.
AI-assisted message replies: Siri can compose contextual replies in Messages using the conversation, personal information and web searches. Shortcuts can also automate replies to selected contacts, although manual Siri-assisted replies allow users to check and edit the response before it is sent.
If you haven’t got Siri AI yet find out how here: Why don’t I have Siri AI on my iPhone?
Read about what happened when we made Siri AI Answer all our Messages.
How good is Siri AI?
Siri AI represents a significant improvement over the old Siri, particularly when handling conversational questions, current information, and personal context. It also has a dedicated app where you can see and continue previous conversations, upload images or documents, and more.
Even in our early tests during the beta, Siri AI proved to be much more helpful and useful. 
It’s definitely one of the biggest reasons to upgrade to iOS 27, potentially changing Siri from a basic voice-command system into a more general way of interacting with the iPhone.
Apple’s approach to AI safety also appears more restrained than some rival chatbots, with Siri designed to avoid excessive flattery, pretending to be human, or responding inappropriately to potentially harmful requests.
However, Siri AI is launching as a “beta” feature and still requires a bit of polish. It’s also only available in English at first, with a handful of other languages/regions, arriving in a later update.
Regional Siri AI availability
Siri AI will not initially be available on iPhone or iPad in the EU. It will also remain unavailable in China while Apple works through regulatory issues. The first release only supports the English language, and initially has Expressive Voices for English (UK) and English (US). Several other languages are coming with the iOS 27.1 update in October.
Siri AI compatibility
Siri AI requires an iPhone 15 Pro or later, and the “new expressive voices” feature requires an iPhone 17 Pro or the new iPhone 18 Pro. 


						

							


Apple Intelligence across apps
As well as Siri AI, the enhanced Apple Intelligence will power new features in Apple’s core apps throughout iOS 27. Safari can organize tabs into topics, monitor webpages for changes and even build extensions from natural-language descriptions. Photos gains a new Spatial Reframing edit tools including an upgraded Clean Up feature. Messages, Mail, and Calendar can now understand context, suggest actions and create events from simple descriptions.


						

							


New features coming to apps in iOS 27
iOS 27 brings a mix of major Apple Intelligence upgrades and smaller quality-of-life improvements across Safari, Photos, Messages, AirPods, Passwords, Wallet, and other core iPhone apps. Apple is also making iOS more adaptable to different screen sizes and orientations, which are changes necessary for the iPhone Duo.
Safari
Safari can automatically group open tabs into topics, making related pages easier to find. A new Notify Me feature will monitor webpages and alert you to changes such as price drops or products coming back into stock.
There’s also a new Describe an Extension feature which lets users create custom Safari extensions simply by explaining what they want the extension to do.

				
					

				
			

Apple




Photos
Photos gains significantly more powerful AI editing tools.
Reframe can alter the composition and perspective of an existing photo, while Extend generates new image content beyond the original frame when straightening a horizon or changing the aspect ratio.

				
					

				
			
Apple




Clean Up has also been improved, with Fast and High Quality modes for removing unwanted objects or details. High Quality mode can produce considerably more natural results, although more ambitious edits can still introduce distortions or invented details.
Photos also adds new categories and the ability to save a frame from a video as a full-resolution photo. The resulting HEIF or JPG retains the video’s original resolution, date, and location metadata rather than simply creating a screenshot.
Camera
iOS 27 features a new more customizable camera interface that lets you pin the controls you use most often. For the iPhone 18 Pro, there are also “pro controls” like white balance, shutter speed, and manual focus along with Apple Reference Image, an authentication system designed to prove that a photo or video was genuinely captured on an iPhone and has not subsequently been manipulated.
The new Siri mode in the Camera app is a more convenient and logical way to access the Visual Intelligence features that used to require either a long-press of the camera button or a Control Center button.
Messages

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Messages gets several useful improvements.
You can decide what the microphone button beside the text field does. Under Settings > Apps > Messages > Show in Text Field, it can be set to Record Audio, Start Dictation, or None. Disabling it does not remove either feature: dictation remains available from the keyboard and audio messages remain in the + menu.
Voice-message playback controls are easier to access, while Apple Intelligence can suggest actions based on a conversation, such as creating a reminder, making a note, or finding relevant photos.
Messages in iOS 27 will gains smarter suggested replies that can better reflect the user’s writing style. (This was removed from the iOS 27 beta and wasn’t available at the launch of iOS 27).
Drawing

				
					

				
			
Foundry




A new dedicated Drawing app replaces the old hidden handwriting interface. Accessible from the + menu, it uses the familiar pens, colours and drawing controls found in Notes and Markup, with finished drawings sent as images.
Mail
Mail gains more context-aware smart replies, including responses that can better match the user’s usual writing style.
Apple Intelligence can also surface information from Mail elsewhere in iOS. For example, the Phone app could retrieve a flight confirmation number from an email when you call an airline.
Phone
A new Call Context feature can surface information that may be useful when on a call. Apple says the information is selected according to who you are calling rather than by listening to the conversation. For example, calling an airline could cause iOS to surface the relevant flight confirmation from Mail.
Birthday reminders can also appear when calling contacts whose birthdays are stored on the iPhone.
iPhone Handoff
iPhone Handoff in iOS 27 lets you switch between two iPhones while keeping the same phone number. The number is active on only one iPhone at a time. When you unlock one of the two iPhones, your calls, voicemail, messages—including SMS and RCS—and your Find My location will be linked to that iPhone. 
The feature will work on any iPhone running iOS 27, as long as it has an eSIM. Both phones must use the same Apple Account, with Messages in iCloud enabled and matching FaceTime/iMessage sign-ins. 
You will need a carrier and eligible plan that specifically support iPhone Handoff – an ordinary eSIM plan alone isn’t enough. In the U.S. T-Mobile offers iPhone Handoff for $5 a month and Verizon has announced support for later in 2026. In the U.K. EE has announced that support for iPhone Handoff is coming soon for £5 a month. 
FaceTime
FaceTime gains Dual Capture, allowing the front and rear cameras to be used at the same time during a call.
Passwords

				
					

				
			
Passwords in iOS 27 will fix things for you.

Apple




The Passwords app continues to warn about weak, reused and compromised credentials, but iOS 27 will go a step further by offering to fix some of them automatically.
Using Apple Intelligence, Passwords can visit supported websites, change a vulnerable password and save the replacement credentials. See: Apple got rid of my biggest password headache.
The usefulness of the feature will depend on how widely websites are supported and how well it handles obstacles such as two-factor authentication and unusual account-management interfaces.
Apple removed this ability to detect compromised passwords and replace them from the beta shortly before the release of iOS 27. It’s expected to arrive with a later update. 
Shortcuts
Shortcuts gains Describe a Shortcut, allowing users to create automations simply by explaining what they want to happen.
Apple Intelligence interprets the request and assemble the appropriate actions across supported apps, potentially making Shortcuts significantly easier to use for people unfamiliar with building automations manually.
Calendar
Calendar can create or modify events from natural-language instructions.
Apple says the app can recognize contacts, locations, dates and other event details as users type, reducing the amount of information that needs to be entered manually.
Siri can also create complete Calendar entries for information that is on your screen in that moment, or by taking a picture with the Siri mode in the Camera app.
Image Playground
Image Playground is considerably more powerful and realistic.
Apple says it can create photorealistic images and lets users modify generated pictures simply by describing the changes they want. Individual objects can also be selected, resized, or repositioned.
AI-generated images will include a SynthID watermark identifying them as synthetic content. This particular feature wasn’t available at launch, but Apple has confirmed it is coming later. 
Wallet
Wallet can create custom passes from QR codes.
Users can add their own fields and information to the pass, and passes automatically sync to Apple Watch.
Weather
Weather gets a clearer, more detailed forecast interface, with rearranged information tiles and new 10-day views showing precipitation probability/amount and wind speed throughout each day.
Home app
Apple Intelligence comes to the Home app for compatible HomeKit Secure Video cameras. It can group related camera notifications, describe recorded video and highlight clips that appear particularly noteworthy.
Maps
Apple Maps improves Flyover using higher-quality aerial imagery and Visual Intelligence models.
Apple says this produces sharper architectural detail and more realistic rendering of elements such as individual trees.
Podcasts
Video podcasts become easier to use, with improved controls for switching between watching a podcast and simply listening to it.
Fitness
Workout summaries have been redesigned to make them easier to share.
Users can also hide completed Fitness+ workouts.


						

							


iOS 27 changes beyond the iPhone 
CarPlay
CarPlay gains an audio scrubber, giving drivers and passengers more direct control when moving through audio tracks and other content.
AirPods
iOS 27 introduces several new AirPods features.
A new Custom EQ lets users independently adjust bass, mids and treble using a simple three-band equalizer under Settings > AirPods > Audio and Routing > Equalizer > Custom.
Compatible AirPods also gain improved Precision Finding through Find My, making individual earbuds easier to locate.
Some features require both iOS 27 and compatible AirPods firmware.
Read How to tune your AirPods with a custom EQ in iOS 27.


						

							


Other changes in iOS 27
It’s not only individual apps that are seeing changes.
Home Screen and landscape mode
Apple is making iOS significantly more flexible when dealing with different screen orientations and sizes.
More Apple apps now work properly in landscape, including Health, Home, Music, Weather, and Watch. Dynamic Island and Live Activities can also adapt to landscape orientation. The Home Screen supports extra-large widgets.
These changes could simply improve iPhone usability, but they’re also well suited to Apple’s folding iPhone Duo.
iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 has similarly become freely resizable, with Apple apps dynamically rearranging their interfaces as the window changes shape.
Liquid Glass refinements

				
					

				
			
Apple




Apple says Liquid Glass has been refined for better readability, more uniform refraction and improved contrast. A new slider lets users adjust the look from ultraclear to fully tinted, while updated icons, toolbars, sidebars and window shapes add polish.
Ringtones, alarms and alert volume
iOS 27 finally separates several sound-volume controls.
Instead of one combined Ringtone and Alerts slider, users can independently adjust:
Ringtones
Alarms and timers
Alerts and system sounds
The change is optional. Under Settings > Sounds & Haptics, turning off Match Ringtone Volume reveals separate controls.
Media and call volume continue to work independently as before.
Keyboard
iOS 27 introduces a new quick-paste control above the keyboard.
It lets you paste recently copied text, images or screenshots without having to long-press inside a text field, making everyday copy-and-paste considerably faster.
Apple has also made the Liquid Glass keyboard design more consistent across apps.
Privacy and Find My
iOS 27 introduces the ability to temporarily pause Find My location sharing without notifying the person with whom the location is normally shared.
Recovery and troubleshooting
Apple is also expanding the iPhone’s recovery interface, giving users more options for diagnosing problems and recovering an iPhone without immediately connecting it to another device.


						

							


System changes and how iOS 27 makes your iPhone faster
Alongside the headline AI features, Apple says iOS 27 includes a wide range of under-the-hood improvements designed to make iPhones faster, smoother and more efficient.
Apps can launch up to 30% faster, newly taken photos can appear in the Photos library up to 70% faster, and AirDrop transfers can be up to 80% quicker. External drive transfers should also improve, while updates to network performance and the system-wide search index are designed to make connectivity and finding information faster.
The company has also reworked core technologies including CPU scheduling, display performance and processing efficiency. These changes should benefit older iPhones in particular, with Apple promising smoother performance and more efficient battery use on devices as old as the iPhone 11 and second-generation iPhone SE.
Our testing of the iOS 27 beta supports those claims. On an iPhone 11 Pro Max, Camera launch time fell from 0.98 seconds in iOS 26 to 0.65 seconds in iOS 27, while Maps improved from 3.01 seconds to 1.36 seconds.
Everyday use also feels smoother, with more fluid animations, unlocking, Control Center and app transitions. The phone ran cooler during testing too, which could point to improved system efficiency and potentially better battery performance.
More broadly, iOS 27 appears focused on refinement rather than simply adding new features. Apple says it has addressed dozens of common user frustrations, while changes such as more adjustable Liquid Glass effects are intended to improve readability and general usability.
That focus should make iOS 27 particularly worthwhile for owners of older iPhones, even on models that do not support Siri AI. Those devices still gain performance improvements alongside features such as clipboard tools for the keyboard, independent alarm and timer volume controls, custom Wallet passes, Photos changes, larger widgets, and Liquid Glass refinements.


						

							


Child safety and parental controls

				
					

				
			
Apple




There are lots of improvements to parental controls, including new time allowances for entertainment, games, and social media, and new schedule tools for different times of day or days of the week.
This includes new features like an expansion of the existing “ask to buy” feature for apps to websites. Before a child can view a new website, they’ll have to ask for permission.
Ask to Browse: Ask to Browse will expand the current Ask to Buy feature to the web. Children will need to request permission before visiting new websites, and parents can review requests in Messages before approving.
Communication Safety: Communication Safety continues to help protect children from viewing or sharing nudity in Messages, FaceTime and other apps. Apple says it will also intervene before children see gore or violent content in shared images and videos.
Time Allowances and schedules: Parents can set Time Allowances across categories such as Entertainment, Games and Social Media. Recommendations are based on a child’s age combined with guidance from clinical and child development experts. Schedules let parents choose which apps are available at different times or on different days.
Redesigned Screen Time: Screen Time gets a redesigned interface with an at-a-glance view of average device usage and most-used apps. Apple says parents can quickly limit or extend access in the moment.
Child accounts and family safety: Apple says child accounts remain central to age-appropriate protections. Parents can manage app access, web access, communication permissions and Screen Time settings. 
Problems with Parental Control set up 
Updating the parent’s iPhone is not enough to activate the redesigned Screen Time experience. Apple says every eligible iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch and Vision Pro in the Family Sharing group must be running the appropriate version 27 software.
Devices that cannot run version 27 are listed as Legacy Devices and can continue using the older Screen Time and Family Sharing system. Apple says these incompatible devices should not prevent supported devices from adopting the new controls.
To find out which devices need to be updated go to Settings > Family > View Family Devices. Once eligible devices are running iOS 27, go to Settings > Family > Get Started to transfer the family’s existing parental controls or set up new ones.
Some families have encountered delays, outdated device listings and eligible hardware incorrectly appearing not to have been updated. Apple has acknowledged the rollout problems and says it is working to resolve them. If an eligible device is no longer owned or accessible, Apple recommends removing it from the Apple Account device list.


						

							


Accessibility changes in iOS 27
Accessibility features are smarter and more intuitive in iOS 27:
VoiceOver gives richer image descriptions and better understanding of onscreen content.
Live Recognition lets users press the Action button to ask questions about their surroundings and receive detailed responses.
Voice Control is more intuitive, allowing users to describe onscreen buttons and controls rather than remembering exact coordinate labels or numbers.
Accessibility Reader is able to handle more complex source material and provide summaries and translation.


						

							


iOS 27 compatibility 

				
					

				
			iPhone 11 is supported by iOS 27.
Roman Loyola/IDG




According to Apple, iOS 27 supports iPhones back to the iPhone 11 and second-generation iPhone SE, although some Apple Intelligence and Siri AI features require newer hardware.
Support for iOS 27 does not mean every device gets every feature. Apple Intelligence and Siri AI require an iPhone 15 Pro or iPhone 16 or later, while the most advanced on-device AI models require an iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone Air, or iPhone 18 Pro. On iPad, Apple Intelligence requires an M1-class model or the A17 Pro iPad mini, while the newest on-device models require an M4 iPad with at least 12GB of RAM.
There had been speculation that the iPhone 11 series and iPhone SE 2 would miss out on iOS 27 after leaker Instant Digital claimed on Weibo that the 2019 iPhone 11, 11 Pro and 11 Pro Max, along with the 2020 iPhone SE 2, would no longer be supported. That prediction proved incorrect, giving those models at least one more year of software support.
However, the iPhone 11 generation is nearing the end of its support life. As we explain in our guide to how long Apple supports iPhones, the iPhone 11 Pro and 11 Pro Max have already been added to Apple’s Vintage iPhone list.
The iOS 27 compatibility list is:
iPhone 17e (launched in 2026) 
iPhone 17, 17 Pro / 17 Pro Max (launched in 2025)
iPhone Air (launched in 2025)
iPhone 16e (launched in 2025)
iPhone 16 / 16 Plus and iPhone 16 Pro / 16 Pro Max (launched in 2024)
iPhone 15 / 15 Plus and iPhone 15 Pro / 15 Pro Max (launched in 2023)
iPhone 14 / 14 Plus / 14 Pro / 14 Pro Max (launched in 2022)
iPhone SE 3 (launched in 2022)
iPhone 13 / 13 mini / 13 Pro / 13 Pro Max (launched in 2021)
iPhone 12 / 12 mini / 12 Pro / 12 Pro Max (launched in 2020)
iPhone SE 2 (launched in 2020)
iPhone 11 / 11 Pro / 11 Pro Max (launched in 2019)
The main dividing line for Apple Intelligence remains the iPhone 15 Pro generation: the standard iPhone 15 and all older models can run iOS 27, but they do not support Apple Intelligence.


						

							





 FAQ 


1.
When was iOS 27 released?
iOS 27 was released on September 14, 2026.





2.
Which iPhones get iOS 27?
The iPhone 11 and iPhone SE 2 and newer get iOS 27. However, Siri AI and other Apple Intelligence features require iPhone 15 Pro or newer, and the new more expressive Siri voices feature requires iPhone Air, iPhone 17 Pro, or newer.





3.
Which iPhones will get Siri AI and Apple Intelligence in iOS 27?
The only iPhones that can run Siri AI are the iPhone 15 Pro and Pro Max and any newer generation. If you have a standard iPhone 15 then you won’t get Siri AI and Apple Intelligence.

title: Apple has challenged the $5.7B Taction verdict, arguing jury got it all wrong
content:
A new filing suggests that not only does Apple not violate Taction's patents, but the jury arrived at the record $5.7 billion in damages "based on guesswork" and should be tossed.


Apple is facing a record fine over patents
In April 2021, Taction Technology sued Apple for allegedly infringing on two Taction patents dealing with haptic feedback. It argued that Apple's Taptic Engine used in the Apple Watch was a reverse-engineered copy of the technology.
A jury ruled in favor of Taction in September,  finding that Apple infringed, though not willfully. A new filing from Apple on Tuesday states that not only did the jury award the damages based on guesswork, but that the findings themselves are contradictory.

title: Elevation Lab Pulls AirTag Silencer After Stalking Concerns
content:
Earlier this year, Elevation Lab announced the launch of a "Silencer" for AirTag meant to pierce the speaker on the device to disable the sound.


Elevation Lab explained that it created the Silencer to keep thieves from detecting an ‌AirTag‌ on valuable products like bikes, but the company didn't think easy speaker removal would be problematic.

improved safety features multiple times since the trackers launched in 2021. The latest ‌AirTag‌ 2 even has a louder speaker and more adhesive to make the speaker harder to remove.

Six Colors' Glenn Fleishman, for example, said the device was "appalling." When he asked Elevation Lab about it, Casey Hopkins, the company's CEO, explained that users can already silence AirTags themselves, and people will still get smartphone notifications if an unknown ‌AirTag‌ is traveling with them.

Elevation Lab reversed course and sent out emails today letting customers know that the Silencer is no longer available for purchase.
We launched an AirTag silencing tool recently. We've always made products we want for ourselves, and this was no different - we wanted it for AirTags on our bikes. (Some of us have bikes more valuable than our cars.)

In retrospect though, this also has the side effect of aiding someone with bad intentions to track someone that wouldn't get phone notifications.


The Silencer had a pin located where the ‌AirTag‌ speaker is. The device description instructed users to remove the ‌AirTag‌ battery, apply the Silencer, and hit it with a hammer to cause the pin to pierce the ‌AirTag‌'s plastic cover and the speaker below.

title: Latest macOS beta: What’s new and should you install it?
content:
Macworld





Apple released macOS 27 Golden Gate on September 14, 2026, but development hasn’t stopped. Just two days later on September 16, Apple issued the first developer beta of macOS 27.2, beginning testing of the operating system’s next major point update. Yes, that’s macOS 27.2, not macOS 27.1. 
The macOS 27.2 beta gives developers and testers early access to Apple’s latest fixes, refinements and any features that weren’t ready for the initial Golden Gate release. 
However, as with any beta software, it may introduce bugs, compatibility problems and poorer battery life so we recommend caution if you wish to install it.
Here’s everything you need to know about the latest macOS beta, including what’s new, when the next public beta is likely to arrive and whether you should install it.


What’s the latest macOS beta? 
Apple offers two beta streams: a developer beta and a public beta. The public beta allows enthusiasts and early adopters to test upcoming changes before they are released to everyone. You need to join Apple’s Beta Software Program to access it.
The latest Mac beta is macOS 27.2 beta 4, which Apple released to registered developers on October 13, 2026.
The corresponding macOS 27.2 public beta will be available soon. Public betas usually follow developer betas, although Apple does not guarantee a particular schedule.
macOS 27 Golden Gate beta version tracker 
Apple released macOS 27.2 Golden Gate Developer Beta 4 on October 13, 2026.
The macOS 27.2 Golden Gate Public Beta 3 arrived on October 7; new versions are usually released a day or two after the new developer beta.
macOS 26 Tahoe beta: Apple may continue updating macOS 26 Tahoe with security and maintenance releases, but macOS 27 is now the current operating system and the focus of Apple’s beta program.


						

							




macOS 27 Beta timeline


ReleaseDate
Beta 1June 8, 2026
Beta 2June 22, 2026
Beta 3July 6, 2026
Beta 3 v.2July 13, 2026
Beta 4July 20, 2026
Beta 5August 10, 2026
Beta 6August 17, 2026
Beta 7August 24, 2026
Beta 8August 31, 2026
Release Candidate 1September 9, 2026
Public Beta 1July 13, 2026
Public Beta 2July 22, 2026
Public Beta 3August 11, 2026
Public Beta 4August 17, 2026
Public Beta 5August 24, 2026
Public Beta 6August 31, 2026
Final ReleaseSeptember 14, 2026
macOS 27.2 developer beta 1September 16, 2026
macOS 27.2 developer beta 2September 21, 2026
macOS 27.2 developer beta 3October 5, 2026
macOS 27.2 developer beta 4October 13, 2026

 






What’s new in the latest beta?

				
					

				
			
New features in macOS 27.

Foundry




Apple has not announced any major consumer-facing additions in macOS 27.2 beta 4. The following changes are expected though:
Bug fixes and performance improvements: Addressing issues in the first release of macOS 27.
Additional Siri AI languages: Apple has said the Siri AI will expand to French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish in October. 
Automatic password changes: The promised feature that automatically changes compromised passwords has not yet been implemented, but it could arrive in macOS 27.2.. 
We’ll update this section as changes are discovered.
See Apple’s developer website for more information about the beta. 


						

							


Should you install the macOS beta?

				
					

				
			
Apple




Installing the macOS beta lets you test Apple’s next round of features, fixes and refinements before their public release. Most Mac users should remain on the standard version of macOS 27, particularly if they rely on their Mac for work.
Install if…
You need to test apps
You want early access to new features
You have a secondary Mac available
Wait if…
This is your primary work machine
You rely on niche or specialist software
Stability is critical to your workflow


						

							






Who are you Should you install?

A developer testing appsConsider the developer beta
An enthusiast with a spare MacConsider the public beta 
General user with one MacStay on macOS 27

 






What are the risks of installing beta software?
Installing pre-release software on a primary device carries several risks.
System instability: Performance problems, freezes, crashes, and other unexpected behavior are common during beta testing.
App failures: Third-party applications may crash, behave unpredictably, or stop working entirely.
Hardware strain: Early beta builds can increase battery drain and cause Macs to run hotter than usual.
Data loss: Software bugs may corrupt files, and downgrading to a stable version often requires a complete system reset.


						

							


Safety precautions and best practices
If you decide to install the beta, take the following precautions:
Use a secondary device: Avoid installing beta software on your primary Mac or on any machine used for critical work.
Create a full backup: Use Time Machine to create a complete backup before upgrading so you can restore your Mac if something goes wrong. Note that this needs to be a Time Machine backup from before the beta was installed and you will lose anything saved subsequently.
Install on a separate volume: Consider installing the beta on a separate volume or external SSD rather than replacing your main operating system.
Check storage space: Make sure you have at least 15GB of free storage available before beginning the installation.


						

							


How to install the macOS beta

				
					

				
			
Foundry




The process for installing a macOS beta depends on whether you are seeking the Developer Beta or the Public Beta. Apple simplified this process a few years ago, removing the need for a paid developer account to access early builds. 
The first step is to join Apple’s beta testing program. We explain how to do that in a separate article.
You will need to register your account either as a public beta tester or as a developer in order to enable beta updates on your Mac.
To install the beta follow these steps:
Back up your Mac: Before installing any pre-release software, it is critical to prepare your Mac to avoid data loss. Beta software is inherently unstable and can cause crashes or app compatibility issues. 
Register your account either as a public beta tester or as a developer in order to enable beta updates on your Mac:
For the Public Beta: Visit the Apple Beta Software Program website, sign in with your Apple ID, and agree to the terms.
For the Developer Beta: Register as an Apple Developer on Apple’s website, download the Apple Developer app from the App Store, sign in with your standard Apple ID, and complete the free registration process.
On the Mac where you wish to install the beta, open System Settings and navigate to General > Software Update.
Click the (i) info button next to Beta Updates.
Enable Beta Updates.
The beta will appear as an available upgrade. Select the macOS beta you want to install (e.g., macOS Public Beta or Developer Beta).
Click Upgrade Now to begin the download and installation.
As long as you are a registered developer or enrolled in the public beta program, when the relevant macOS Beta becomes available, it will also show up on your Mac.
Once you are running the beta, the updates will come through to your Mac automatically; you just need to go to Software Update in System Settings and click to install. See How to install macOS.


						

							


How to get a free Apple developer account
If you just want a free Apple Developer account so you can access the beta, you can get this via Xcode or the Apple Developer app in iOS. Here’s how to do it via the Apple Developer app on an iPhone:
Get the Apple Developer App from the App Store. 
Open the app on your iPhone. 
Tap on Account. 
Tap on Sign In. 
Sign in using your usual Apple ID. 
If you wish to actually publish applications to the App Store or receive support, you’ll need to pay $99/£79 per year for a paid account. You can compare the free and paid accounts here.


						

							





 FAQ 


1.
Who can run the macOS beta?
Anyone can run the macOS beta, but to do so, you do need to register for either the developer beta, the public beta, or both.
Apple offers both developer and public beta programs for macOS, enabling all interested users to test pre-release versions of the operating system. While both betas provide early access to new features, they cater to different user profiles based on technical expertise and risk tolerance. Beta software tends to be buggy so the more stable public beta version may be preferable, but even that will not be bug-free.
In the past, the developer beta was only available to developers who had paid to join Apple’s Developer Program (which costs $99/£79). However, for a couple of years now, Apple has opened up the developer beta to registered developers with free developer accounts. We explain how to get a free developer account below. 
If you decide you no longer want to run the beta version of macOS read this: How to remove the macOS beta.





2.
macOS public beta vs developer beta
Since 2023, the Developer Beta has been available to anyone who registers as a developer, even if they aren’t a paid-up member of Apple’s Developer Program. As a result, people with a basic free developer account can download the new macOS developer beta (we show you how to register below).
Whether you should download the developer beta if you aren’t a developer is another question. We don’t recommend you install the developer beta if you aren’t a developer. Instead, our recommendation is to use the public beta (the first version of which usually arrives in July).
There are a few differences between the public and developer betas. The public beta is not the same as the beta that is released through the developer program. The public beta typically launches after the developer beta has undergone initial testing and refinement
Developers get updates to their beta first, and possibly more frequently. But you should keep in mind that betas are by nature not stable, and because the public beta comes after the developer beta it could be a little safer to install. 
The most significant difference is probably the motive of the testers: Developers usually have the aim of ensuring their apps work when the updated macOS is released to the general public, while public beta testers are essentially helping Apple detect bugs and offering feedback on the features. Because of this, developers may get to test new features not available in the public beta. 
If you want to get the public beta the first thing you need to do, if you haven’t already, is join Apple’s beta programs read this for more information: How to become an Apple beta tester.





3.
Is the macOS beta stable?
By its nature, a beta has the potential to be unstable. Therefore, it’s not advised that you install it on a Mac that you rely on. If you have a second Mac that isn’t mission-critical, then install it there. We strongly recommend that you don’t risk all by putting the macOS beta on your primary Mac, especially not in the early days of the beta development. 
If you don’t have a second Mac, there are a couple of ways you could run macOS beta on your Mac without running the risk of losing data or finding your Mac stops working:
We recommend installing it on a partition, which these days is really a volume (and is much easier to create than a partition was). Read about how to do that here: How to dual-boot Mac: Run two versions of macOS on a Mac.
Alternatively, you could install the macOS beta on an external drive and run it on that.
We discuss the safety of the macOS beta and the risks you might be taking in more detail in a separate article.





4.
How to prepare your Mac for the beta
Update your software: We recommend you have the latest full version of macOS installed, although Apple says that the macOS Developer Beta Access Utility requires macOS 10.8 or later.
Make space: We’d recommend at least 25-30GB of available space because the macOS betas tend to be very large. If you end up requiring more space, read: How to free up space on Mac. Note that we always recommend that you have at least 10% space free on your Mac at any time, so if you don’t have that, expect problems!
Back up: Before you install a beta on your Mac, you should make a backup of your data and files. You can find out how to use Time Machine to back up your Mac. We also have a round-up of suitable backup solutions.





5.
How to send feedback to Apple
Should you come across an error or a bug, you should use the Feedback Assistant app to provide feedback to Apple. Launch the app and follow the appropriate steps, selecting the area about which you’re providing feedback and then any specific sub-area. Then describe your issue in a single sentence, before providing a more detailed description, including any specific steps that reproduce the issue. You’ll also be able to attach other files.
You’ll also have to give permission for the Feedback Assistant app to collect diagnostic information from your Mac.
It won’t always be obvious whether something is a bug or just not as easy to use as you might have hoped. Either way, if your feedback is that something appears to work in an illogical way, Apple will want to know that.
If you are having trouble with a third-party app, you can let Apple know by reporting it through the 3rd-party Application Compatibility category in the Feedback Assistant. However, we’d suggest that you also provide feedback to the app’s developer, who will no doubt be grateful.





6.
Will I be able to update from macOS beta to the final version?
Beta users can move to the finished release once its build is newer than – or equivalent to – the beta installed. Read: How to leave the macOS beta.  





7.
Can I talk about the beta publicly?
According to Apple and the license agreement all beta testers must agree to, the beta is “Apple confidential information”. By accepting those terms, you agree not to discuss your use of the software with anyone who isn’t also in the Beta Software Program. That means you can’t “blog, post screenshots, tweet, or publicly post information about the public beta software.”
However, you can discuss any information that Apple has publicly disclosed; the company says that information is no longer considered confidential.





8.
How to downgrade from the macOS beta
You can always revert to an earlier version of macOS, though depending on how you back up, it’s not necessarily a painless process.
Start by making sure the data on your drive is backed up, then erase the drive and install the latest public version of macOS. When you first start up your Mac, you can use the Migration Assistant to import your data from the backup. Here’s a more detailed tutorial on downgrading from the macOS beta and we also have a tutorial on downgrading to an older version of the Mac OS.





9.
Is the beta free to download? 
Yes, the macOS beta is free to download for both developers and the general public. Apple offers two distinct tracks for testing pre-release software: the Developer Beta and the Public Beta, both of which are now accessible without a paid subscription.





10.
Can I go back to the stable version?
Yes, you can go back to the stable version of macOS from a beta, but the complexity of the process depends on whether the final version of that software has been released yet.
If you are running macOS 27.2 beta and want to return to the current public release of macOS 27, simply turning off Beta Updates will stop future beta installations, but it will not immediately downgrade the Mac. To return before Apple releases an equivalent public build, you may need to erase the Mac and reinstall macOS, then restore data from a backup made before installing the beta.





11.
Should I install the beta on my main Mac?
Installing a macOS beta on your primary computer is generally not recommended due to the inherent risks of using unfinished software. While beta programs offer early access to new features, they are designed for testing and often contain significant bugs that can disrupt your daily workflow.





12.
Do I need an Apple Developer account to install the beta?
You do not need a paid Apple Developer account to install the macOS beta. While access to developer betas was previously restricted to those paying a $99/£79 annual fee, Apple changed this policy in 2023 to allow anyone with a free developer account to access these builds. Alternatively, you can join the Public Beta program, which is also free and accessible to anyone with a valid Apple ID.





13.
How often are new beta versions released?
New macOS beta versions are typically released every one to two weeks, with the frequency increasing as the final public release date approaches. The beta updates refine features and address bugs identified by testers.





14.
Is the macOS beta safe to install?
The beta is generally safe to test, but it may contain bugs that cause crashes, poor battery life, app compatibility issues, or data loss. Always back up your Mac before installing.





15.
Will my apps work with the macOS beta?
Many apps will work normally, but some third-party software may crash, perform poorly, or not launch at all until developers release updates.
